title: Speech, stone tool-making and the two-step evolution of language. Experimental protocols.
author: Dana M Cataldo

steps_raw.instruction: Speech, stone tool-making and the two-step evolution of language.
Dana Michelle Cataldo, Andrea Bamberg Migliano, Lucio Vinicius

Training of subjects and execution of flintknapping sessions followed a written protocol strictly followed by a skilled tutor. The general protocol is presented as well as its treatment-specific variants.

Welcome the participant to the study. Present a copy of the consent form to each participant: “Please read this consent form and then if you agree to participate in the study, sign at the bottom of the form”. If the participant signs the consent forms, ask: “Do you have any questions about the study?”
Present each participant with: goggles, gloves, coat for protection, breathing mask, selection of flint, selection of hammerstones.
Tutor: “This experiment’s aim is to provide a better understanding of how language contributed to the evolution of stone tool technologies and cumulative culture in the hominin language.”
Introduction phase: “Now we will begin the introduction phase of this experiment.” Hand the participant the introduction sheet, demonstration flakes, and stick.
Tutor: “Please read the sheet to gain a better understanding of flint tools and their use and then try out this flake on this stick to get a better understanding of what makes a useful flake.”
After 5 minutes, say: “That ends the introductory phase.” Take the information sheet, the flake, and the stick from the participant.

Teaching phase (full language, gesture and speech groups): “Now we will begin the Teaching phase of this experiment. In this part of the experiment the tutor will explain how to make the flakes that you just saw.” Instruct and assist the participant using full language/gesture/speech.

Teaching phase (control group): “Now we will begin the Teaching phase of this experiment. In this part you will have access to cores and flakes produced by a tutor. We will ask you to examine them so that in the next phase you can recreate as many viable flakes as possible.” Place the demonstration core and flakes in front of the participant, providing no instruction.
After 5 minutes: “That ends the Teaching phase. From this point on, you will get no further instruction on how to make flakes.”

Testing phase: “Now we will begin the Testing phase. In this part of the experiment you will be asked to make as many viable flakes as possible. Please choose a flint core from this pile and choose a hammerstone from the selection. You can stop at any time if you feel you made as many viable flakes as you can.”
After 20 minutes, or whenever the participant is done: “Please stop knapping” OR “Thank you for knapping.”
Classifying phase: “Now please classify your flakes as viable or non-viable, and place them in two separate piles.” This concludes the Testing phase of the experiment.

Questionnaire: “Now we would like for you to rate your received instruction and how it helped you making flint tools. The questionnaire asks you to rank your agreement with three statements on a scale from 1 to 5.” Present the participant with the Post-Test Questionnaire.

Tutor: “On behalf of UCL, thank you all very much for participating in this assessment. We hope that you learned some new information regarding flint knapping and have a better foundation if you want to continue to learn it in the future. Have a great day!” Collect the Post-Test Questionnaire. Collect all flakes and cores made by the participant and place in a plastic bag registering participant ID and condition.
